correctness.rationale: Both generating polynomials follow from explicit complete finite sums over selected vertices; subtraction yields an exact cubic factor and all cumulative threshold differences. The two possible complements of a cubic six-vertex graph are a six-cycle and two triangles, proving the exhaustive sharp classification. Admissibility 2d | n gives minimal n=6 when d>=2. A standalone exact-integer verifier independently recomputes each graph's 64 subsets, verifies the symbolic difference, and exhausts all 5005 labelled nine-edge graphs, of which exactly 70 are cubic. The self-contained proof does not infer a general statement from incomplete experiments.

value.rationale: The counterexample gives a definitive negative answer to a sharply posed new extremal question. It occurs at the smallest possible admissible order, resolves the complete cubic six-vertex threshold phase diagram and identifies a mechanism—the failure of nonnegative-weight generating-function domination to imply cumulative coefficient domination—that is mathematically useful for revising the extremal conjecture. It is not merely a routine unmotivated small invariant or a known-table restatement.
